title: Relative navigation benchmark on real data: KISS-ICP lidar odometry, OpenVINS VIO, mono and nadir VO, scored with evo
summary: One command per part. KISS-ICP (pip) on KITTI odometry 04 from the raw drive, scored against KITTI odometry GT and OXTS; OpenVINS v2.7 stereo-inertial (ROS 1 serial mode, Docker, arm64) and an OpenCV mono VO baseline on UZH-FPV indoor_forward_3; frame-to-frame nadir VO over 9 km of VPAIR light-aircraft imagery at about 320 m AGL, image-only versus attitude-aided with a yaw-bias sensitivity. Every trajectory is written as TUM and navdash/1 JSONL for templates/demo-dashboard, and the fitted scale / heading / noise of each odometry is plugged into the altpnt-integrity sample as its relative source.
verified: Ran on 2026-11-06, Apple M2 Max, python3.12 venv (kiss-icp 1.3.0, evo 1.38.1, opencv 5.0.0.93, rosbags 0.11.9) and OpenVINS v2.7 built from source in a ros:noetic-perception arm64 image under colima (4 vCPU). KITTI 04: KISS-ICP ATE 0.23 m, KITTI t_rel 0.41 %, final drift 0.12 % of 394 m. UZH-FPV indoor_forward_3 (49.5 s GT window, 278 m): OpenVINS ATE 0.36 m, final drift 0.26 %; mono VO with a GT scale oracle ATE 0.80 m. VPAIR (199 frames, 8.98 km): image-only nadir VO 15.5 % final drift, attitude-aided 0.65 %, 3.2 % with a 2 deg yaw bias. altpnt-integrity rerun with each fitted error model. 5 unit tests pass. EuRoC, ORB-SLAM3, cuVSLAM and KITTI 07 were not run (see README).
